advisories.title: The deferred-or-rides ledger carries four of integration v4's five external rides; the DR-103 schema dependency is absent
advisories.finding: Integration v4's identityDependencies lists six entries. ID-DEP-N2 (DR-117/DR-010), N3 (DR-116), N4 (DR-114) and N5 (DR-111) are now all carried, and N6 is this row's own catalogue. ID-DEP-N1 — 'Canonical manifest schemas and stableId field', ridesOn DR-103, consequence 'This row consumes the declared stableId. It does not author the schema.' — appears nowhere: DR-103 occurs zero times in the artifact. Once the ledger is read as the inventory of what DR-104 parks elsewhere, carrying four of five reads as completeness it does not have.
advisories.whyOnlyAdvisory: The artifact's stated scope is D-012's decided policy, the eleven classes, the execution remainder and the D-012 deferred items. N1 is not a D-012 deferral — it is an upstream input dependency — so it sits outside that scope, which is exactly why Codex graded the analogous N5 gap an advisory rather than a SHOULD-FIX. I am matching that grade rather than escalating a sibling of a finding the corpus already priced.
advisories.repair: Add an obligation in the shape of OBL-RIDES-DR111 — for example OBL-CONSUMES-DR103, leftoverDesign false, rideStanding consumes-DR-103-schema — citing ID-DEP-N1, with a matching 'Does not retarget DR-103' refusal. Alternatively state in the summary that the ledger carries only rides arising from D-012 deferrals and named class ownership, which would make the omission principled rather than apparent.

consideredAndDeclined.item: Escalating the DR-103 omission to SHOULD-FIX on the ground that it is the same shape as the DR-116 gap I charged at v1
consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: The shapes match but the scopes do not. DR-116 was a D-012 deferral, named in D-012's own clause and in D-130's explicitlyDeferred list, and the artifact's purpose expressly undertakes to split the D-012 deferred items. DR-103 is an upstream consumption dependency recorded only in v4's identityDependencies. Charging it as a blocker-grade omission would hold the artifact to a scope it never claimed.

consideredAndDeclined.item: Whether I should have raised the DR-111 ride myself at v1
consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: Not a matter for declining — recorded plainly: I should have. I enumerated D-130's explicitlyDeferred list at v1 and found the DR-116 gap, but I did not enumerate integration v4's identityDependencies, which is where DR-111 and DR-103 both live. Codex caught DR-111. Running that second enumeration this round is what surfaced DR-103.

independence.priorParticipation: I rejected v1 on the DR-116 gap and Codex accepted it while raising the DR-111 advisory. Each of us saw one thing the other missed, and both came from the same class of check — enumerating a pinned source's own inventory. I ran both enumerations this round.
independence.biasNote: Raising a fresh advisory in the same family as one I missed carries a risk of overcorrection. I tested it on scope rather than on symmetry: DR-103 is genuinely absent and genuinely outside the artifact's stated remit, which is why it is an advisory and not a finding that blocks.

coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with one advisory. Thirteen attacks run, one landed and it is advisory-grade. Custody holds: v2 at cdb3003b and frozen v1 at 48d418b6, both 0444 and unmoved, dispatch and prompt agreeing, HEAD stable at 23fe6d9, file 08 at 3a9442d1 equal to the subject's own pin, governing tree clean. Both dispositions land and I verified each against primary bytes rather than the disposition block. My SHOULD-FIX produced OBL-DEFERRED-DR116 exactly as specified — leftoverDesign false, deferred-to-DR-116, filed under deferredOrRidesElsewhere, with a matching non-retargeting refusal — and its two grounds hold: D-012's clause routes the support/vulnerability side to DR-116 and D-130's corpus lists it in explicitlyDeferred. Codex's advisory produced OBL-RIDES-DR111, which checks out against integration v4's ID-DEP-N5 and is genuinely DR-104's business, since multi-version coexistence is one of the eleven classes. The change is strictly additive: two obligations added, none removed, the leftover set unchanged at OBL-NT-11-EXECUTION alone, an eight-way partition with no overlap, and the fixture audit re-run from scratch at eleven classes, seventeen files, zero mismatches. All four recorded D-012 deferrals are now carried, which closes the gap I charged at v1. The advisory is that the rides ledger now carries four of the five external rides integration v4 records: ID-DEP-N1, the DR-103 schema dependency, is absent and DR-103 occurs zero times in the artifact. I graded it advisory rather than SHOULD-FIX on scope — N1 is an upstream input dependency, not a D-012 deferral, which is the remit the artifact claims, and it is the same grade Codex gave the analogous N5 gap. One disclosure: I found the DR-116 gap at v1 by enumerating D-130's explicitlyDeferred list but did not enumerate integration v4's identityDependencies, which is where both DR-111 and DR-103 live. Codex caught DR-111. Running that second enumeration this round is what surfaced DR-103.
